steps.tx: **Corynebacterium diphtheriae** is a pleomorphic gram positive bacillus that arranges in Chinese letter and palisade patterns. It does not spore, does not move, and grows aerobically. A lysogenic beta phage supplies the toxin that creates diphtheria: pseudomembranous pharyngitis, bull neck, myocarditis, and neuropathy. The disease is now rare where toxoid vaccination holds and returns where coverage lapses.
steps.say: Diphtheria bacilli are pleomorphic gram positive rods in Chinese letter arrangements, aerobic, and non motile. Phage borne toxin builds the throat membrane and can injure heart and nerves. Toxoid vaccination keeps the disease rare until coverage falls.

vis.alt: An open throat shows a grey adherent pseudomembrane coating the tonsil and spreading toward the palate.
vis.caption: A grey adherent membrane coats tonsil and adjacent pharynx, the local lesion of respiratory diphtheria. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The **Albert stain** paints granules bluish black and bacilli green (Albert I toluidine blue and malachite green, Albert II iodine), metachromatic volutin (Babes Ernst) granules at poles on Loeffler slope grown organisms. Its positive smear supports but never proves diphtheria without toxigenicity.
steps.say: Green rods with black polar granules support diphtheria; toxin testing convicts.

left.title: Albert technique
points: Granules best in young serum cultures

right.title: Interpretation
points: Culture before antibiotics, antitoxin before culture results
Notify public health immediately on suspicion

steps.tx: The **Albert stain** colours bacilli green and granules bluish black. Albert I contains toluidine blue and malachite green, and Albert II is iodine. Metachromatic volutin, the Babes Ernst granules, sits at the poles of organisms grown on a Loeffler slope. A positive smear supports diphtheria but never proves it. Toxigenicity testing is still required before the strain is convicted.
steps.say: Albert stain turns diphtheria bacilli green and their polar volutin granules bluish black, best after growth on Loeffler medium. The smear supports the diagnosis. Only a toxin test proves the strain.

vis.alt: A light micrograph shows green bacilli with bluish black granules at the poles.
vis.caption: Albert stained rods appear green with bluish black polar granules after growth on Loeffler medium. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Antitoxin first** is diphtheria's therapeutic law: equine diphtheria antitoxin neutralises only unbound toxin, given on clinical diagnosis after sensitivity testing, antibiotics (penicillin or macrolide) eradicating organism and toxin production, airway secured (membrane obstructs), contacts cultured and prophylaxed, case isolated droplet. Waiting for culture loses myocardium.
steps.say: Antitoxin on sight, antibiotics behind it, airway above all: hours decide myocardium.

nodes.label: Airway secured, ENT and critical care
Antitoxin after test dose (do not wait culture)

steps.tx: **Diphtheria toxin mechanism** (A B exotoxin, ADP ribosylation of elongation factor 2) halts protein synthesis in heart, nerve, kidney and mucosa, the AB toxin archetype of the pharmacology toxin lessons, encoded by tox gene on beta corynephage so non toxigenic strains colonise harmlessly until phage converts them.
steps.say: One enzyme shuts off EF2 in heart and nerve; the gene arrives by phage.

left.title: Toxin mechanics
points: B binds, A ADP ribosylates EF2
Protein synthesis arrest and cell death

right.title: Clinical timing
points: Antitoxin only neutralises circulating free toxin

steps.tx: **Other corynebacteria** (diphtheroids) graduate from contaminants by site and repetition: jeikeium (multidrug resistant, device and neutropenic sepsis, vancomycin susceptible), urealyticum (struvite urinary stones, urease), pseudotuberculosis and ulcerans (zoonotic, ulcerans can carry toxin and cause diphtheria like disease, now outnumbering classic in some countries).
steps.say: Diphtheroid on one plate is skin; jeikeium in neutropenic blood is a vancomycin problem.

left.title: Coryneform cast
points: C urealyticum: alkaline urine and stones
C ulcerans: cattle and pets, toxigenic possible

steps.tx: **Vaccination architecture** (DTaP childhood, Td and Tdap adult, toxoid not anti colonisation) prevents toxin disease while carriage persists in pockets, so outbreaks exploit coverage gaps and adult waning; toxigenic culture from contacts, chemoprophylaxis (erythromycin, penicillin) and immunisation of contacts close an introduced case's circle.
steps.say: Toxoid stops toxin, not carriage; adult boosters are diphtheria's forgotten perimeter.

left.title: Vaccine facts
points: No effect on carriage prevalence direct

right.title: Outbreak responses
points: Culture and tox test cases and close contacts

steps.tx: **Cutaneous diphtheria** (tropical ulcers colonised by toxigenic strains, punched out chronic sores) seeds respiratory disease and community spread in crowded and homeless outbreaks, culture of skin lesions mandatory in suspected clusters, systemic toxin complications rarer but real. Skin is diphtheria's quieter reservoir.
steps.say: Chronic punched ulcers can carry diphtheria silently into communities.

left.title: Cutaneous portrait
points: Chronic non healing ulcers with membrane

steps.tx: **Laboratory biosafety and notification** complete: diphtheria is immediately notifiable, isolates referred for toxigenicity, laboratory exposures assessed (aerosols), and Schick replaced by antitoxin antibody levels where immunity documented for health workers. The bench treats this organism as public health specimen, not routine throat flora.
steps.say: Notify first, refer the isolate, protect the bench: diphtheria is never routine.
